correctness.rationale: The enumerator and deepest-coset formulas are correct. Internal incidence constraints force arm constants, and endpoint incidence enforces even parity. Nearest distance is the sum of local minority weights, except in the absence of a tied block when the preferred parity is odd: then it costs an extra L−2 max(a_i). Tied words and the two untied parity classes yield the displayed polynomial after division by 2^(m−1). For L=2s a no-tie odd word with deficits t_i=s−a_i≥1 has distance ms−sum(t_i)+2min(t_i)<ms; for L=2s+1 equality at ms+1 in the corresponding bound requires every deficit to vanish. An independently written full-word calculation reproduces all four finite spectra, including coefficient vectors (1,8,13,8,2) and (1,12,66,163,189,81) for (4,2) and (4,3); replay: branches/526dd565-1112-495a-a67c-2114b31e85fc/independent_coset_bruteforce.py (output in the corresponding .out file). The correctness defect is in the unrestricted channel corollary and its proof in RESULT.md lines 31–34 and 83: the claim gives no message distribution and the proof assumes all-zero may be sent without loss for any tie rule. At p=1/2, the valid deterministic ML rule always outputting a fixed codeword has conditional success 1 for that word and 0 for the others, whereas the formula gives 1/|C|. The formula is correct for uniformly averaged block success with arbitrary ML tie-breaking, or conditional on any fixed word with translation-equivariant ML syndrome decoding. The missing qualification does not affect the distance distribution.
